dedupe_keys.name: critical materials monitor columbia university center on global energy policy

description: An online tool that maps supply chains of critical materials for the energy transition. The methodology page says it follows each material through upstream mining, midstream processing and downstream products, using UN Comtrade trade data for 2017 to 2022 by HS code and reserve and production figures from the USGS, the British Geological Survey, World Mining Data and the OECD, collected in May 2024, to show country shares and trade dependencies. The tool is free to use in a browser. Coverage is global, by country. Caveats: HS codes group some materials together, and the page read does not give a licence or a download. For simulation it gives concentration and trade dependency for lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths and other materials, to model supply shocks from export restrictions or disruptions in a few producing countries. A related catalogue record is the Chatham House resourcetrade.earth database.
